Hi Jane,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning to walk through MedCare's use case. Quick recap and concrete next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we heard:
- You plan to send patient intake forms and clinician notes to the model for summarization and routing (will include PHI).
- Primary requirements: a signed BAA, SOC 2 evidence, ability to restrict PHI to a non-multi-tenant environment, and customer-managed encryption keys if possible.

Short answers / eligibility notes:
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers handling PHI. We provide a standard BAA template (attached) and we can consider minor redlines.
- Eligible deployment modes for PHI: Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC / on-prem) are eligible for PHI processing. Our public hosted multi-tenant API is limited to non-PHI / de-identified data only.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report available; we typically share the report under an NDA or via our secure Portal. I attached the report PDF for your review.
- Encryption & KMS: For Dedicated we support cloud KMS integrations and BYOK workflows; for Private we support customer HSM/KMS options.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send our vendor security questionnaire back to you with answers and the SOC 2 + BAA template attached (see attachments).
2) Loop in our Security/Infra folks for a short technical scoping call to confirm networking and KMS requirements (I will loop Michael and Dev below).
3) If the BAA language looks OK, we'll route the agreement through legal and propose timelines for execution.

Can you confirm:
- Approx timeline for when MedCare needs the BAA signed?
- Any specific KMS/HSM vendor you're expecting to use (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / on-prem HSM)?

Happy to schedule a quick 30-minute follow-up later this week to run through the attachments.

Marissa - quick answers below, happy to join the call with MedCare if you schedule it.

- BAA: Our standard BAA covers Dedicated and Private deployments for PHI processing. We have clauses covering access controls, breach notification, and data segregation. Minor redlines are usually OK; anything substantive we'll escalate to Legal. (Attached: Redwood_BAA_Template.docx)

- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report (attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Report_2025.pdf). The report covers our inference control plane and serving runtime used in both Hosted and Dedicated offerings. For Private/on-prem deployments there are certain customer-controlled components that are out of scope (we call those carve-outs) - we can document the carve-outs clearly for MedCare.

- KMS/HSM: For Dedicated we support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and a BYOK flow where customers can bring keys into their cloud KMS. For Private/on-prem we support customer-managed HSMs and can integrate with on-prem KMS where the customer retains key custody. I've attached a short note that we can share with MedCare describing the BYOK steps.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Report_2025.pdf; Redwood_BAA_Template.docx; Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Partial.pdf
